decisions.what the ink shows: The base consists of two parallel bars, without the humps of m. The attached small s curls down beside the right end and extends just below the lower bar. Resolve the glyph to the equals abbreviation and represent the low right s literally, instead of C’s raised s or H’s expanded word.

The canceled/overwritten lower cluster at the second G has a central descender and side strokes suggesting psi, but its upper strokes merge with G and the cancellation. Alpha remains possible; retain uncertainty in the struck ink.

The capital I, tall t strokes, looped p descender, short intervening letter strokes and final nt ligature support Interprétant. The reading shared by C and H is retained confidently; only H’s certainty wrapper differs.

The beginning just- is clear. A long crossing/final flourish obscures how the low ending strokes divide. Juste is favored but the longer ending remains possible, so uncertainty is added over the complete word.

The f descender, tall l and h, accent and ending traces support flèches, but a thick horizontal strike covers the small central letter bodies. Every letter cannot be independently isolated, so the struck word receives an uncertainty wrapper despite the two witnesses agreeing on its reading.

notes.text: The page defines the complementary arc/edge sets in (53) and introduces the quotient notations (54). It describes G as obtained from G-prime by contracting the selected edges, or corresponding arcs, to points, and explains this in terms of continuous maps between topological realizations. It states that the amalgamated sum (52) exists for any subgraph with the same vertices, then begins a bracketed assertion that every generalized graph morphism factors uniquely, stopping at “en un”. The geometry/topology and flèches/arêtes revisions are retained, along with the canceled uncertain lower symbol at the second subgraph occurrence. Upper ink pagination reads 21 and lower pencil pagination reads 43; their authorship is not independently inferred. This is a reading summary, not a verification of the asserted existence or factorization.

main_review_note: The main reader inspected the whole scan and all twelve crops. The arrow over a-prime has a pointed right end unlike the wave over C-prime; the subgraph dot is distinctly below the separate prime. The equals abbreviation has two bars and a small right-hand s curling below the lower one. The underline ends before G-prime. The cancellation obscures central letters of flèches and the lower subscript cluster, so those uncertainties remain. The ending of juste is favored but not forced; its whole-word alternative is retained. The numeral 21 is at the head, and lighter 43 at the foot; no attribution of the pagination is assumed.
